newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY COACH VOGTS CALLS IN FRESH FACES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY COACH VOGTS CALLS IN FRESH FACES.

text.p: Germany coach Berti Vogts, alarmed by a string of below-par performances, nominated three new players on Tuesday in his squad for next week's World Cup qualifier against Ukraine.
Vogts named Bayer Leverkusen libero Jens Nowotny and midfielders Sven Kmetsch and Jens Jeremies, of Hamburg and 1860 Munich respectively, for the match in Bremen on April 30.
The European champions scraped a 3-2 win over Albania this month in their last qualifier and drew their previous two group nine games against Portugal and Northern Ireland.
"I wasn't satisfied with one or two players. So there are a few new faces this time," Vogts said.
Nowotny's form for Leverkusen has been one of the main reasons for their outstanding league campaign this season. The club are just three points behind leaders Bayern Munich.
Although national team libero Matthias Sammer is out with a groin strain, Nowotny is unlikely to play against Ukraine from the start. Bayern's Thomas Helmer will probably replace Sammer.
Goalkeepers: Oliver Kahn (Bayern Munich), Andreas Koepke (Marseille).

Defenders: Markus Babbel (Bayern Munich), Thomas Helmer (Bayern Munich), Juergen Kohler (Borussia Dortmund), Jens Nowotny (Bayer Leverkusen), Stefan Reuter (Borussia Dortmund), Thomas Schneider (VfB Stuttgart), Christian Woerns (Bayer Leverkusen)

Midfielders: Mario Basler (Bayern Munich), Dieter Eilts (Werder Bremen), Joerg Heinrich (Borussia Dortmund), Jens Jeremies (1860 Munich), Sven Kmetsch (Hamburg), Andreas Moeller (Borussia Dortmund), Michael Tarnat (Karlsruhe), Dariusz Wosz (Bochum), Christian Ziege (Bayern Munich).
Strikers: Oliver Bierhoff (Udinese), Fredi Bobic (VfB Stuttgart), Sean Dundee (Karlsruhe), Juergen Klinsmann (Bayern Munich).
